title.narrative: Building a Blue-Green Economy in St. Kitts and Nevis

description.narrative: 1. The project's investments in science, training, private sector opportunities, and in creating the framework for the NOP-SAP and the Coastal Master and Spatial Management Plan will the following direct benefits:2. The project supports the NOP-SAP process that, through its implementation, will add to the suite of climate adaptation measures in more resilient marine resources and important steps towards water security. The investment program will add tangible next steps to the SAP implementation. The science created under Component 1 will provide important baselines and will support actions that support the two islands coastal and marine systems, e.g. coral reefs and mangroves that mitigate the effects of sea-level rise. Private sector engagement and connecting businesses to technology options will increase business opportunities that will add to the SKNs economy. That concept is further solidified by vocational training that will lead to job opportunities. The small grant projects are designed to provide local opportunities. The project, in coordination with CHO-IP, also provides skill training to national professionals that will lead to future opportunities, nationally and internationally, which is important for Small Island Developing States. The project's development of an investment portfolio will define future projects, such as in fisheries and aquaculture, are preliminary steps in expanding the Blue Economy of St. Kitts & Nevis. Collectively, these will support a sustainable Blue Economy and reduce vulnerabilities. 3. We confirm that the project design has considered socio-economic benefits to be delivered by the project and these have been clearly described in the Project Description and will be monitored and reported on during project implementation (at MTR and TER).
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

To address ocean hypoxia by tackling the root causes and drivers of land-based nutrient pollution in St. Kitts and Nevis, through policy reforms, regulatory measures, sustainable financing, and nature-based solutions
